scope: One bounded source-correspondence check of C's R56 mu-linked T_R/B_act argument and R57 alpha > eta denominator domain. This is not full geometric or certificate validation.

checks.details: The English text preserves X = mu - xi, Y = upsilon + mu, the actual supports, B_act = 2 mu - b(tau) + lambda(tau) D, and D >= 2 mu - b(z). It retains B_act >= B_z + 2(1 + lambda(tau))(mu - 1), followed by upsilon >= B_z - 1 - lambda(tau) X + (1 + 2 lambda(tau))(mu - 1) > B - 1 - lambda(tau) X_*. Thus it does not infer the second coordinate bound merely from B_act > B, and it keeps both bounds attached to the same actual T_R.

The English text states a > alpha > eta before deriving V(a), and proves alpha > eta on eta in [3/10,3/8], tau in (0,1/5] through the positive endpoint bounds of -19 eta^2 + 10 eta - 1. It retains D = 1 - alpha, 0 < D <= 407/600 < 1, 0 < X < 1, -1 < P < H_* < 1, and A > a > alpha > eta. The positive denominator for V(A) is therefore justified on actual configurations. Its certificate construction preserves T_d > 0, Q_d > 0, M > 0, N > eta M and explicitly does not require these configuration-dependent signs at arbitrary relaxed parameter points. It also preserves the source's allowance of auxiliary A > 1 without treating A as a physical angle.

limitations: Source and English exposition were compared. No claim is made that the underlying certificate files, polynomial coefficients, global premise transfer or geometric theorem have been independently validated.
